
# Run from simulated data

**Default Knit runs the experiment:** construct the design, generate fresh samples,
perform the Ky–Fan permutation tests, and summarize the rejection decisions.
The default is the full manuscript design with $R=B=1000$, so it can take substantial
time. Run the examples below from the repository root; the smoke example is a short execution check.

No existing observations, result CSVs, or `data/` directory are required for simulation.
Keep the repository structure intact: scripts in `simulation/`, modules in `R/`, and reports in `reports/`. Rendering requires `rmarkdown`, `knitr`, and Pandoc;
statistical calculations use base R. Relative parameter paths resolve from the repository root.

`R` counts independently generated sample pairs per scenario; `B` counts permutations
within each test. `profile="manuscript"` covers 180 scenarios and two orders, hence
360 result cells. `profile="archive"` runs the explicitly defined extended design
with 1,020 result cells; the name is retained for compatibility and does not read
archived results when `mode="rerun"`.

```{r usage, eval=FALSE}
# Short execution check; these estimates are not manuscript results.
rmarkdown::render(
  "reports/01_reproduce_tables.Rmd",
  params = list(mode = "rerun", profile = "smoke", R = 20, B = 99),
  output_file = "01_reproduce_smoke.html"
)

# Full manuscript experiment: 180 scenarios, k=1 and k=3, R=B=1000.
rmarkdown::render(
  "reports/01_reproduce_tables.Rmd",
  params = list(mode = "rerun", profile = "manuscript", R = 1000, B = 1000),
  output_file = "01_reproduce_full.html"
)

# Extended experiment: 360 scenarios and 1,020 result cells.
rmarkdown::render(
  "reports/01_reproduce_tables.Rmd",
  params = list(mode = "rerun", profile = "archive", R = 1000, B = 1000),
  output_file = "01_reproduce_extended.html"
)
```

`mode="archived"` remains an explicit saved-results viewer. Only that mode requires
`data/table_archive.csv`; it performs no simulation and supports `manuscript` or
`archive` profiles. Its output is labeled as saved results.

# Simulation design

Each group contains $m$ independent, zero-mean observations in $p$ dimensions with
covariance $\Sigma$. Transform $W=\Sigma^{1/2}Z$ using the **symmetric positive-definite
square root**.

| Code | Standardized vector $Z$ |
|:---|:---|
| N | Independent standard normal coordinates |
| T | $\sqrt{6/Q}H$, $Q\sim\chi^2_8$, $H\sim N(0,I_p)$; one shared $Q$ per observation |
| E | $\sqrt{E}H$, $E\sim\operatorname{Exp}(1)$; one shared mixing variable per observation |
| G | $\sqrt{V}H$, $V\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(3,1/3)$, with scale $1/3$; one shared mixing variable per observation |
| L | Independent standard logistic coordinates scaled by $\sqrt{3}/\pi$ |

| Covariance | Definition |
|:---|:---|
| C1 | $I_p$ |
| C2 | Entry $(i,j)$ is $0.5^{|i-j|}$ |
| C3 | First five diagonal entries are 4; the rest are 1 |
| C4 | First block has size 4; remaining blocks have size 2; each block is $0.4I_d+0.6J_d$ |

The 15 distribution pairs comprise five identical-distribution and ten different-distribution
pairs. All satisfy the equal-covariance $H_0$; only identical-distribution pairs are
exchangeable controls. These experiments estimate rejection rates under $H_0$, not power.

The main tables use $(p,m)=(10,50),(10,150),(40,150)$ and $k=1,3$. The extended profile
uses the following orders, each crossed with C1–C4 and all 15 distribution pairs:

| $(p,m)$ | Orders $k$ |
|:---|:---|
| $(10,50),(10,150)$ | 1, 3 |
| $(20,50),(40,50)$ | 1, 2, 3 |
| $(20,150)$ | 1, 2, 5 |
| $(40,150)$ | 1, 2, 3, 5 |

Sample covariances use denominator $m-1$ and recomputed group means. For the covariance
difference $D=\widehat\Sigma_X-\widehat\Sigma_Y$, let $|\lambda|_{(j)}(D)$ denote the
$j$th largest absolute eigenvalue. The statistic is

$$T_k=\sqrt m\sum_{j=1}^{k}|\lambda|_{(j)}(D).$$

Each independent permutation uniformly selects $m$ pooled raw observations for the
first group. The upper-tail p-value and rejection rule are

$$\widehat p_k=\frac{1+\sum_{b=1}^B\mathbf 1\{T_{k,b}\geq T_{k,\mathrm{obs}}\}}{B+1},
\qquad \text{reject if }\widehat p_k\leq\alpha.$$

Within each scenario and replicate, all $k$ share data and permutations. Covariances
computed from group sums and second moments are algebraically equivalent to `cov()`.
Replicate seeds depend on the master seed, scenario, replicate, and purpose; execution
order and worker count do not affect results.

# Construct the experimental scenarios

The grid is defined in code from the design above. No result table is used to infer
which experiments should be run.

```{r scenario-grid}
run <- .workflow$slads_execute_workflow("tables", params)
grid <- run$grid
table_data <- run$table_data
result_dir <- run$result_dir
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Item = c("Profile", "Scenarios", "Scenario/order result cells",
           "Requested repetitions R", "Requested permutations B", "Nominal level"),
  Value = c(params$profile, nrow(grid),
            sum(lengths(strsplit(grid$ks, ",", fixed = TRUE))),
            params$R, params$B, params$alpha)
))
```

# Optional fixed reference

Leave `reference_csv: ""` to simulate without reference results. To compare with a
fixed table, set `reference_csv` to its path. The CSV must contain `p`, `m`,
`covariance`, `pair`, `k`, and the rate column selected by `reference_rate_column`.
Set `reference_R` to the number of repetitions used for that reference table.
An explicitly supplied missing or malformed file is reported before simulation starts.
A reference must also be outside the current run directory so that rerunning cannot
overwrite it; a different historical run directory is allowed.

The existing `data/manuscript_reference.csv` contains the **later completed rerun**,
not the earliest table. In the preserved historical `new_vs_archived.csv`, the earlier
table is in **`archived_rate`** and the later rerun is in `rejection_rate`. To compare
with that earlier table, select `reference_rate_column: "archived_rate"` and
`reference_R: 1000`. The reference is read only and is never replaced by new estimates.

```{r optional-reference}
if (is.null(run$reference_info)) {
  cat("No reference supplied. Simulation requires no saved results.\n")
} else {
  cat("Fixed reference:", run$reference_info$path, "\nRate column:",
      run$reference_info$rate_column, "\n")
}
```

# Run and save results

A simulation run saves configuration, source hashes, replicate p-values and rejection
indicators, summary CSVs, and session information, with checkpoints every 10 replicates.
Matching inputs and configuration permit resumption; `resume: false` recomputes the run.
The run identifier includes the entry script or report and loaded R modules. Text edits also change it,
so use the frozen source snapshot to resume an older run. Reference data are not used
to generate samples or determine rejection decisions.

`workers` defaults to 1 and is capped at 7, with one BLAS/OpenMP thread per worker.
Windows runs serially. Existing reference files and manuscript sources are not modified.

```{r run}
cat("Source:", run$provenance, "\nOutput directory:", result_dir, "\n")
```

# Rejection rates and Monte Carlo uncertainty

For $s$ rejections in $R$ successfully completed repetitions,

$$\widehat q=s/R,\qquad
\operatorname{MCSE}(\widehat q)=\sqrt{\widehat q(1-\widehat q)/R}.$$

The summary includes pointwise 95% Wilson intervals. `rate_minus_alpha` is the estimated
rejection rate minus the requested nominal level; it is a descriptive diagnostic, not
an automatic pass/fail test. A small smoke run checks execution only.

```{r simulation-summary}
if (!is.null(run$diagnostics)) {
  knitr::kable(head(run$diagnostics, 12), digits = 4)
} else {
  cat("Saved table view: archived estimates used R=B=1000 and alpha=0.05.\n")
}
```

# Tables

Entries are rejection rates (Monte Carlo standard errors). Simulation results use the
requested configuration. Unrun scenarios in smoke or partial designs remain dashes;
no saved values are inserted into newly computed tables.

```{r tables, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
groups <- unique(table_data[c("p", "m", "k")])
for (i in seq_len(nrow(groups))) {
  g <- groups[i, ]
  cat(sprintf("\n\n## p=%d, m=%d, k=%d\n\n", g$p, g$m, g$k))
  tab <- .workflow$format_paper_table(table_data, g$p, g$m, g$k)
  print(knitr::kable(tab, align = c("l", rep("c", ncol(tab) - 1L))))
}
```

# Optional comparison with the fixed reference

The comparison preserves every new result, including scenarios without a reference
match. Differences are **new rate minus reference rate**. The combined MCSE below
assumes independent simulations. It is not a tolerance for identical random streams,
and agreement within it does not establish exact reproduction of an earlier run.
Exact reproduction also requires the matching implementation, random streams, and
simulation configuration. The earliest historical experiments cannot be reconstructed
from their rounded table entries alone.

The selected reference file, its hash, the selected rate column, and the assumed
reference repetition count are saved in a separate `reference_comparisons/` directory.
Different reference inputs produce separate comparison directories.

```{r differences}
if (!is.null(run$comparison)) {
  cat("Comparison directory:", run$comparison_dir, "\n")
  knitr::kable(head(run$comparison, 30), digits = 4)
} else {
  cat("Reference comparison skipped.\n")
}
```
